correctness.rationale: The complete four-letter source-pair language has eight explicitly listed pairs, and every length-26 binary factor is one of 256 windows in the 32-letter substituted source-pair blocks. All source pairs occur. The included independent exact checks of each window determine the smallest equal-Parikh block root up to 13, yielding the 256-entry histogram and the sharp four templates. The substitution is primitive (every third image contains all letters); its four letter frequencies are 1/4, and the unique eight pair frequencies are 1/8 by the half-interior/half-bridge recurrence. Thus every aligned template has density 1/256. A separate arithmetic Rudin–Shapiro generator checks 65,536 symbols against the entire 200-factor language. All hypotheses, offset boundaries, and quantifiers cover every starting index without extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected treatments study automatic-word factor predicates (Schaeffer–Shallit), Rudin–Shapiro abelian factor complexity (Lü–Chen–Wen–Wu), or abelian-square-richness of other words (Fici–Mignosi–Shallit). None gives a bound for the minimum abelian-square root at *each* Rudin–Shapiro start or its eight-atom exact density spectrum. Their statements do not imply the new conditional local distributions: lengthwise Parikh-class counts discard adjacency and positions, while distinct-square richness need not constrain a prescribed start. Existing exact eight-source-pair factor covers are credited as previous methods, not claimed as a discovery. Targeted exact-bound and alias searches found no indexed equivalent for the first-root histogram or density law; priority remains unverified for unindexed sources.

value.rationale: Abelian squares are a standard and motivated local repetition invariant. A uniform starting-position guarantee is substantially more precise than global factor abundance: the sharp smallest root 13, the unexpected sparse spectrum {1,2,3,4,8,11,12,13}, and the exact eight-atom natural density law classify a natural canonical 2-automatic word. The density-1/64 rare sharp cases are mathematically informative because they distinguish worst-case positions from typical ones. The result stands as a complete local classification even without a theorem for more general automatic words.
